# To the Bedrock

> A portfolio site by Robert Andersson (PhD) of interactive tools and visualisations about complexity, emergence, and the friction between how organisations describe their work and how that work actually behaves.

## Site facts

- Author: Robert Andersson, PhD.
- Built with plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (D3.js for interactive visualisations) — no framework runtime.
- Structure: Home (identity/orientation), Catalogue (interactive modules, each with local section numbering), Notes (narrative context and reflections), Articles (long-form argument-driven writing), Site Notes (colophon/meta).
- The author also designs and ships production software: ioths, a privacy-first offline-first Markdown note-taking app for iPhone and iPad, live on the App Store.

## Catalogue modules

- Emergence — Conway's Game of Life and a GANTT-chart variant, showing local rules producing global patterns.
- The Garbage Can Model — an interactive implementation of Cohen, March & Olsen's 1972 organisational-choice-under-ambiguity model, with taxonomy, exploration, and assessment tools.
- Learning & Feedback (Epistemic Bets) — the assumptions an organisation makes about when it can know enough to decide, and feedback debt when evidence can't revise those assumptions.
- Products Over Projects — product-mode versus project-mode as a residual-risk distinction, grounded in ISO 31000, COSO ERM, PMI risk management, and related frameworks.
- Flow & Queuing — queueing theory and the resource-utilisation trap, using D3 visuals for load, variability, backlog, and flow.
- Boundary-free monitoring — a viewport-as-AOI remote-sensing proof of concept using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery.
- Ambiguous Documents — how ambiguous product documentation becomes precise enough to test and build.
